Teḥinah Imahot for Shabbat Mevorkhim by Leah Horowitz in her Yiddish translation (ca. 1790) with its posthumously expanded adaptation

tei:div.tei:head: Teḥinah Imahot for Shabbat Mevorkhim by Leah Horowitz in her Yiddish translation (ca. 1790) with its posthumously expanded adaptation

tei:lg.tei:l: Master of the World, you created heaven and earth and all creatures with great compassion within six days and with only ten words. And on the seventh day, which is Shabbat Qodesh, you rested from your work. And you also commanded your beloved people, Yisrael, that they, too, should rest on Shabbat Qodesh from all work, and also refrain from speaking words which are not words of Torah, which each person should study according to his ability. And women, too, should know how to perform their obligations that God has commanded.

You have also given us new moons which the Sanhedrin used to consecrate. And today, when we consecrate and bless Rosh Ḥodesh on the Shabbat before the Rosh Ḥodesh, it is a time to entreat God. Therefore we extend our hands to you, Hashem yitbarakh, in supplication, and pray that you will return us to Yerushalayim and renew our days as of old. For we do not have a Beit haMiqdash now, nor an altar, nor a Kohen Gadol to absolve us, but only our prayer, which is a substitute for the sacrifices. Therefore, may you accept and answer our prayer.

Answer us this month, through the merit of our mother Sarah for whose sake you commanded and said: “Do not dare to touch my anointed ones,” which means: Do no evil to my anointed people, and do no harm to my prophets.
And may the merit of our mother Rivqah, who caused our father Yaaqov to receive the blessings from his father Yitsḥaq, cause the blessings to be fulfilled soon through her children Yisrael.

And may the merit of our faithful mother Raḥel, to whom you promised that through her merit her children Yisrael would be delivered from exile, cause the promises to be fulfilled. For when Yisrael was led into exile, they passed not far from the grave in which our mother Raḥel lies. Yisrael begged the enemy to allow them to go to Raḥel’s grave, and there they began to weep and to cry out: “Our dear mother, how can you watch us being led into exile?”

Then Raḥel went up to Hashem yitbarakh with a bitter cry and said, “Master of the World, your compassion is certainly much greater than the compassion of a human being. You, who are certainly a merciful and gracious God, surely have compassion.” God answered her: “You are right. I will take your children out of their misery.” Thus we ask that this may come to pass for her merit.
And for the merit of our mother Léah and that through her merit you may illumine our eyes so that we may overcome darkness.
Since we are called Bnei Avraham, the children of Avraham our forefather, how is it then that we are still so neglected?
Wash me thoroughly; continue to wash me of my sins. Therefore renew us and bring us a new and joyful month [so peace and prosperity will return to us, and all will be good].
Source of our strength, you are our great Lord: raise us up high and cause only good to come to us. May all be turned to good through the merit of our holy forefathers, Avraham, Yitsḥaq, and Yaaqov.

May it be your will, Hashem, our elo’ah and elo’ah of our ancestors, that you renew for us this month and cause good and blessing to come to us, and that you give us a long life, a good life, and a blessed life, that we may be nourished by God — blessed be He.
Give us a life of ample sustenance, with pleasure and not with anxiety, a life of strong bodies, that our bones may become strong.
Give us a life of awe of Heaven, that our children may believe in God — blessed be He — and walk in God‘s path, so that their own paths may be to good fortune.
Give us a life without shame or dishonor, that I may not be ashamed, either in Olam haZeh (This World) or in Olam haBah (the World-to-Come) before the Heavenly Court.

Give us a life of wealth and honor, that we may raise our children to Torah, to the Wedding Canopy (Ḥupah), and to Good Deeds (Maasim Tovim). As King David — alav hashalom — prayed: “Master of the World, let me die like a king and not like a pauper.”

May we be granted a life filled with love of Torah and awe of Heaven. May my children believe in God — blessed be He — as did the children of Yaaqov our forefather — alav hashalom. For when Yaaqov was about to die, he wished to reveal the final redemption but lost the ability to prophesy and was afraid. He said to his children: “Perhaps there is among my children one who is evil.” And they responded: “Shema Yisrael, Hashem our elo’ah, Hashem is One,” which means, Listen, our father Yisrael, God who is your God is also our God and is One.
Grant us our request and cause good to come to us by merit of the prayers of many generations. Amen, selah.

tei:note.tei:p: Mishnah, Avot 5:1; this refers to the ten-fold “And God said”’s in Genesis 1 and 2.
